spec.title: `flow:sync-from-code` — reconcile specs with code when code changes first

p.PACKAGE-INSTALLS-THE-SYNC-FROM-CODE-PROT: A vibevm `flow` package that installs the **Sync-from-Code** protocol into a project.

p.SYNC-FROM-CODE-IS-THE-EXCEPTIONAL-PATH-O: The normal information flow in a spec-driven project is top-down (head → WAL → spec → code); Sync-from-Code is the *exceptional* path for closing spec drift when code moves before the spec.

p.two-legitimate-situations-lead: Two legitimate situations break top-down flow:

facts.SITUATION-THE-USER-EDITS-CODE-DIRECTLY: The user edits code directly in the editor because it's faster than articulating the intent to the agent first.
facts.SITUATION-THE-USER-GIVES-AN-IMPERATIVE-C: The user gives an imperative command in chat ("change the timeout to 600 s") and the agent edits code without touching the spec.

p.in-both-cases-the-spec-is-now-wrong-and-: In both cases the spec is now wrong; left unreconciled, the next session reads the stale spec, concludes the code is in error, and "fixes" the code back — correctly by the spec-wins rule, wrong in outcome.

p.THE-FLOW-IS-THE-SANCTIONED-WAY-TO-CLOSE-: This flow is the sanctioned way to close that gap.

p.package-contents-lead: This package ships three pieces of content plus a boot snippet:

facts.CONTENT-THE-FULL-PROTOCOL: `spec/flows/sync-from-code/SYNC-PROTOCOL.xml` — full protocol: what Sync-from-Code is, when to run it, what the draft spec diff must contain (value + reason + revisit trigger), and what it explicitly does not do.
facts.CONTENT-THE-DECISION-TABLE: `spec/flows/sync-from-code/when-to-apply.xml` — decision table: *should I run it right now?*, including the cases where you should **not** (temporary hacks, mechanical changes, unnamed reasons).
facts.CONTENT-THE-REVIEW-CHECKLIST: `spec/flows/sync-from-code/review-workflow.xml` — human-side checklist for the approval step: six checks that catch bad syncs before they land.
facts.CONTENT-THE-BOOT-SNIPPET: `spec/boot/20-flow-sync-from-code.xml` — boot snippet loaded at session start, pointing the agent at the protocol.

p.UNINSTALL-REMOVES-EVERY-FILE-THE-PACKAGE: Uninstalling removes every file the package wrote, including the boot snippet.

facts.COMPOSES-WAL-AND-ATOMIC-COMMITS-BY-DISTI: Works with `flow:wal` (`10-…`) and `flow:git-atomic-commits` (`30-…`): numeric boot-snippet prefixes are distinct by design.
facts.COMPOSES-WAL-FOR-THE-SESSION-END-UPDATE: A successful sync *may* trigger a WAL update; that update goes through `flow:wal`'s session-end hook, not this flow.
facts.COMPOSES-ATOMIC-COMMITS-FOR-THE-COMMIT-M: A sync ends in a `docs(spec)` commit; message formatting is pinned by `flow:git-atomic-commits`.

p.extracted-from-the-books-third-chapter: The protocol is extracted from *AI-native development*, chapter 3 (*"Архитектура памяти"*, subsection "Протокол Sync-from-Code").

p.short-version-spec-driven-projects-need-: Short version: spec-driven projects need a named, rare, human-approved path for the inverse flow; without one, drift accumulates silently and the spec stops being authoritative.
